lead: Find out in two minutes which social benefits you may be entitled to, and prepare the application right away.
sample: This is an example. Replace the values with your own details. Everything stays on your device, nothing is sent.
trans: The names of benefits and offices stay in German so you can use them when you talk to the authorities. The translations are machine-made and may contain errors.

young.label: Children aged 18 to 24 in training or studies

cb.kinder12: A child is 12 years or older
cb.unterhalt: The other parent pays no child support or too little
gruppe.label: Age of the oldest adult
ausb.label: Is anyone in training or studying?

rules.sum: How the check works and where the values come from
rules.intro: The check compares your details with the limits set by law. It is a guide only and does not replace an official decision.
rules.de: The details are in German, as in the laws.
rules.src: The values come from statutes and advice portals and should be professionally reviewed before wide use.
foot.1: Important: This check gives a first estimate. It is not legal advice and not an official decision. The responsible office decides on your claim.
foot.2: Free help with filling in forms is available from welfare associations such as VdK and SoVD and from advice centres of Caritas, Diakonie and AWO.
f.intro: Enter your details. You get an informal application letter, a data sheet and a document list to print. Your data stays on your device.
f.name: First and last name
f.none: No benefit to prepare right now.
f.pick0: Please choose at least one benefit.
f.copyFail: Copying did not work. Select the text below and copy it by hand.
f.deNote: The letter and the data sheet are in German because the offices need them that way. You can hand them in or send them as they are.
f.stichtag: For many benefits an informal application secures the starting month. You send the official form afterwards.
h.ausschluss: Excluded by a benefit you receive
h.schonGrund: You already receive a basic security benefit
h.butMoeglich: Possible if another benefit is approved
n.but: Education and participation package for children
n.gsa: Basic security in old age or with reduced earning capacity
zu.uvg: Unterhaltsvorschussstelle (in the Jugendamt, youth welfare office)
t.kindergeld.ja: You get {kg} per month for each child until the child is 18, or up to 25 if in training or studies.
t.kindergeld.na: Report changes such as the end of training or a move to the Familienkasse.
t.kindergeld.keinKind: Child benefit is paid for children up to 18, and up to 25 if in training.
t.wohngeld.ausschluss: People who receive Grundsicherungsgeld or basic security from the authorities do not get Wohngeld. The rent is already covered there.
t.wohngeld.na: Apply for the extension in good time. Report changes in income, rent or household.
t.wohngeld.verm: With substantial assets there is no Wohngeld. Guide value for household size {n}: about {limit}. The Wohngeldstelle decides each case individually.
t.wohngeld.hoch: Your gross income is above the Wohngeld limit.
t.wohngeld.grenzeStufe: Limit (household size {n}, rent level {stufe}): about {lo} to {hi} gross per month, depending on deductions.
t.wohngeld.grenzeOhne: Limit (household size {n}): about {lo} to {hi} gross per month, depending on rent level and deductions.
t.wohngeld.ja: Your income is below the Wohngeld limit.
t.wohngeld.vielleicht: You are in the borderline range. The Wohngeldstelle calculates deductions and allowances exactly.
t.wohngeld.stufeUnbekannt: Your rent level is unknown, so the check calculates cautiously.
t.wohngeld.zuNiedrig: Wohngeld requires a minimum income. Your income probably does not cover living costs and rent. In that case basic security is often the right benefit. You can still apply for Wohngeld.
t.kiz.keinKind: The Kinderzuschlag is only paid for children who get Kindergeld (under 25 years).
t.kiz.ausschluss: Kinderzuschlag and basic security exclude each other. The children are already covered there.
t.kiz.na: Apply for the extension in good time. It is usually granted for six months.
t.kiz.minEink: For the Kinderzuschlag you need at least {min} gross per month. With less, Grundsicherungsgeld is more likely.
t.kiz.zuHoch: Your income is so high that probably nothing is left of the Kinderzuschlag.
t.kiz.zuNiedrig: The Kinderzuschlag is meant to prevent the need for basic security. If income is too low for that, Grundsicherungsgeld fits better. You can still apply.
t.kiz.ja: Your income is in the right range. Maximum: {max} per child and month.
t.kiz.rand: You are near the upper limit, a small amount may remain. Maximum: {max} per child and month.
t.ggeld.sozialamtZustaendig: From the standard retirement age, or with permanent full incapacity to work, the Sozialamt is responsible, not the Jobcenter. See Grundsicherung im Alter.
t.ggeld.na: Report changes to the Jobcenter and apply for the extension in good time.
t.ggeld.sozialamt: You already receive basic security or social assistance from the Sozialamt. You cannot get both.
t.ggeld.verm: Financial assets above about {schon} have to be used first. The protected amount depends on age.
t.bedarfJa: This is what your household needs to live by law, including rent: about {bedarf} per month. Your income is below that.
t.bedarfRand: This is what your household needs to live by law, including rent: about {bedarf} per month. Your income is just below or above. The office calculates allowances and deductions exactly.
t.bedarfNein: This is what your household needs to live by law, including rent: about {bedarf} per month. Your income is above that. Check whether Wohngeld fits.
t.but.keinKind: The education package applies to children and young adults up to 25 in school or training.
t.but.inhalt: It includes {schul} school supplies per year, {teil} per month for sport, music or culture, lunch at daycare and school, and school trips.
t.but.bezug: You already receive a suitable benefit, so you are entitled to it.
t.but.folgt: Anyone who receives Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag or basic security is also entitled to the education package.
t.but.moeglich: The claim depends on receiving Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag or basic security.
t.but.fehlt: The education package goes to families receiving basic security, Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag or social assistance. According to your details this probably does not apply.
t.uvg.keinKind: Unterhaltsvorschuss is paid for children under 18.
t.uvg.unterhalt: Unterhaltsvorschuss is paid when the other parent pays no child support or too little. You did not state this.
t.uvg.zwei: Unterhaltsvorschuss is for single parents. It ends if you marry or live with the other parent. With a new unmarried partner it can continue.
t.uvg.ab12: From age 12 it is only paid if the child does not depend on Grundsicherungsgeld or you earn at least {min} gross.
t.uvg.ja: Amount per month: up to 5 years {a}, 6 to 11 years {b}, 12 to 17 years {c}. Child support actually paid is deducted. At most until the 18th birthday.
t.gsa.voraus: Basic security in old age is paid from the standard retirement age or with permanent full incapacity to work. You stated neither.
t.gsa.na: Report changes in pension, rent or assets to the Sozialamt and apply for the extension in good time.
t.gsa.ggBezug: You receive Grundsicherungsgeld from the Jobcenter. At the retirement age, or with permanent incapacity to work, the Sozialamt takes over.
t.gsa.verm: Financial assets above {schon} have to be used first. A home you live in yourself or a reasonable car do not count.
t.bafoeg.keine: You did not state anyone in school, training or university.
t.bafoeg.keinKind: You did not state a child in the household.
t.bafoeg.kindJa: The parents' income is below the allowance of about {fb} net per month. BAföG is paid for university, vocational colleges and certain schools, for example if the child does not live with the parents.
t.bafoeg.kindRand: The income is above the allowance of about {fb} per month. BAföG is then reduced but can still be paid. The office calculates exactly.
t.bafoeg.kindNein: The income is well above the allowance of about {fb} per month. Probably nothing is left.
t.bafoeg.ich: BAföG depends mainly on the parents' income, which this check does not ask for. In some cases it does not count. Have the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung calculate it.
t.bafoeg.vermHoch: Your assets are above the limit of {verm}.
t.bafoeg.alter: As a rule BAföG is only paid if you are at most 45 when the training starts, for some courses younger. Ask the office.
t.pflege.keiner: You did not state a care level. Anyone who needs lasting help in daily life can apply to the Pflegekasse for a care level.
t.pflege.antrag: A care level has been applied for or might be possible. The Pflegekasse arranges an assessment. From care level 2 there is Pflegegeld if relatives provide the care.
t.pflege.pg1: With care level 1 there is a relief amount of {ent} per month for help in daily life. Pflegegeld starts at care level 2.
t.pflege.pg2: Pflegegeld for care at home: {geld} per month at care level {pg}. In addition there is the relief amount of {ent} per month.
z.ggBezug: You receive Grundsicherungsgeld (until June 2026: Bürgergeld). Wohngeld and Kinderzuschlag usually do not go with it. The education package often runs through the Jobcenter.
z.wgKiz: Wohngeld and Kinderzuschlag can be combined. Apply for both, even if one of them is borderline.
z.gsaWg: You cannot receive Grundsicherung im Alter and Wohngeld at the same time. Have both checked and ask which route is better for you.
z.ggVsWg: Grundsicherungsgeld excludes Wohngeld and Kinderzuschlag. Have both checked and ask which route is better for you.
z.kgZuerst: Apply for Kindergeld first. Without Kindergeld there is no Kinderzuschlag.
z.stichtag: Many benefits are only paid from the month of the application. Apply early, even informally.
z.keine: According to these details no benefit fits for sure. If income, rent or household change, check again. A social counselling service can name further help.
s.kindergeld.wo: At the Familienkasse of the Federal Employment Agency, mostly online.
s.kindergeld.u1: Tax identification numbers of parents and child
s.kindergeld.u3: For children over 18: certificate of training or studies
s.kindergeld.tip: Kindergeld is paid back for six months at most. Apply soon.
s.wohngeld.wo: At the Wohngeldstelle of your municipality, city or district. Applying online is often possible.
s.wohngeld.u1: Rental contract or confirmation of rent
s.wohngeld.u2: Proof of income for all household members, usually for the last 12 months
s.wohngeld.u3: ID documents and details of everyone in the household
s.wohngeld.tip: Wohngeld is paid from the month the application arrives, not backdated. Apply early.
s.kiz.wo: At the Familienkasse, online. There is an official pre-check, the KiZ-Lotse.
s.kiz.u2: Proof of the parents' income, usually for the last 6 months
s.kiz.u3: Details of rent and heating costs
s.kiz.tip: The Kinderzuschlag usually runs for 6 months. After that you need a new application.
s.ggeld.wo: At the Jobcenter of your town or district, in person or online.
s.ggeld.u2: Rental contract and utility bill statement
s.ggeld.u3: Bank statements of the last months and proof of income
s.ggeld.tip: The benefit is paid from the first day of the month in which you apply. Get in touch early.
s.but.wo: At the Kommune (district or city). People who get Grundsicherungsgeld often apply at the Jobcenter at the same time.
s.but.u1: Notice about Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag or basic security
s.but.u3: Invoice or confirmation, for example for club fees or lunch
s.but.tip: Ask in good time, claims lapse after about twelve months.
s.uvg.wo: At the Unterhaltsvorschussstelle, usually in the Jugendamt of your town or district.
s.uvg.u2: Details of the other parent and proof that he or she pays nothing or too little
s.uvg.tip: The office often claims the money back from the other parent. That is not your problem.
s.gsa.wo: At the Sozialamt of your town or district.
s.gsa.u1: Pension notice or proof of other income
s.gsa.u2: Rental contract and utility bill statement
s.gsa.u3: Bank statements and proof of assets
s.gsa.tip: Children are not asked to pay if their income is below {eur:100000} a year.
s.bafoeg.wo: At the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung, for students at the Studierendenwerk. There is an online application.
s.bafoeg.tip: BAföG is paid from the month of the application. Apply before the training starts.
s.pflege.wo: At the Pflegekasse that belongs to your health insurance. A phone call is enough to apply.
s.pflege.u2: Details of what help is needed in daily life
s.pflege.u3: Medical reports or hospital discharge letters
s.pflege.tip: The Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) will visit. Keep a care diary beforehand.
sc.intro: Got an official form? Take a photo of it or paste its text. You will see what each field means and which answer from your check goes there. The app does not fill in the form itself.
sc.paste: Or paste the text of the form
sc.localNote: Default: the photo is read only on your device and sent nowhere. For this, the text recognition downloads a program from the internet once.
sc.claudeNote: Optional: Claude reads the photo more closely. The photo is then sent to Claude and counts toward your Claude usage. Choose only documents you are happy to send.
sc.consent: Yes, the photo may be sent to Claude.
sc.ocrFail: Reading on this device is not available here. Paste the text of the form instead.
sc.claudeFail: Claude could not analyze the form. Try again later or paste the text.
sc.denied: Claude is not allowed or not available here.
sc.rate: Too many requests or your limit is reached. Please try again later.
sc.badImage: This file did not work. Choose a different photo.
sc.need: Choose a photo or paste the text.
sc.noFields: I found no known fields. The photo may be blurry. Otherwise ask an advice center.
sc.res: How to fill in the form
sc.check: Check every entry yourself before you sign. The explanations are a guide, not legal advice.
sc.f.name: Your full name, as on your ID.
sc.f.geb: Your date of birth as day, month and year.
sc.f.adresse: The address where you live and where mail is sent.
sc.f.tel: A phone number for questions. Usually optional.
sc.f.iban: The bank account the money should be paid into. The IBAN is on your bank card.
sc.f.idnr: Numbers such as tax ID or pension insurance number. You find them on letters from the tax office or the pension insurance.
sc.f.haushalt: Everyone who lives with you and shares household costs, with their age and relationship to you.
sc.f.miete: The cost of the home: basic rent, service charges, heating and living space. It is in your rental contract and last statement.
sc.f.einkommen: All money coming into the household: wages, pension, Kindergeld (child benefit), maintenance. Usually gross and net, as on the payslip.
sc.f.vermoegen: Savings, account balances, securities, car, property. List all accounts, even small ones.
sc.f.bezug: Benefits that you or your household already receive or have applied for.
sc.f.unterhalt: Payments from the other parent. Also state it if nothing is paid.
sc.f.ausbildung: School, training or university: institution, start and expected end.
sc.f.gesundheit: Details on disability, care level or reduced earning capacity. Attach the notices as proof.
sc.f.unterschrift: Place, date and your signature. Without a signature the application is often not valid.
t.kiz.verm: With substantial assets there is no Kinderzuschlag. Guide value for household size {n}: about {limit}. The Familienkasse decides case by case.
foot.3: This check reflects the 2026 rules. Changes are planned for 2027, for example for Wohngeld (draft law, not yet passed). Amounts may change at the turn of the year.
bh.person.label: Does anyone in the household have a disability?
bh.gdb.label: Degree of disability (GdB)
bh.blind.label: Can the person see very poorly or not at all?
bh.em.label: Can an adult only work to a limited extent due to illness or disability?
bh.em.unter3: Yes, less than 3 hours a day
bh.em.3bis6: Yes, 3 to under 6 hours a day
cb.bhSelbst: Because of the disability, the person cannot support themselves (no or very low income of their own)
cb.em5: This person has paid into the pension insurance for at least 5 years, 3 of them in the last 5 years
cb.wfbm: The person works in a workshop for people with disabilities
cb.babBetrieb: I am doing a vocational training (apprentice) in a recognised training occupation
cb.babWohnt: Because of the training I do not live with my parents, or I am at least 18, married or have a child
n.kgBeh: Child benefit for adult children with a disability
n.eingl: Integration assistance for people with disabilities
n.pausch: Tax allowance for people with disabilities
n.ausweis: Severe disability card and compensation for disadvantages
zu.eingl: Provider of integration assistance (in Bavaria the Bezirk; for children with a mental-health disability the Jugendamt)
zu.pausch: Finanzamt (tax office), in the tax return
zu.arbeit: Provider of integration assistance (in Bavaria usually the Bezirk)
zu.rundfunk: Beitragsservice of ARD, ZDF and Deutschlandradio
u.arzt: Medical reports, expert opinions or severe disability card
u.steuerid: Tax identification number (for Kindergeld also the child’s)
u.rentenverlauf: Insurance number and details of previous employment
u.bescheide: Notices about other benefits, for example Pflegegeld
u.vertrag: Details of the employer and employment contract
u.beitragsnr: Contribution number of the broadcasting fee
u.haushalt: Details of all people in the household
s.kgBeh.wo: At the Familienkasse of the Federal Employment Agency, in writing or online.
s.kgBeh.tip: Kindergeld is paid retroactively for six months at most. Apply early.
s.emrente.wo: At the Deutsche Rentenversicherung, online, in writing or at an advice centre.
s.emrente.tip: The pension insurance first checks whether rehabilitation can restore the ability to work. Get advice before applying.
s.eingl.wo: At the provider of integration assistance. In Bavaria this is usually the Bezirk. For a child with a mental-health disability the Jugendamt is responsible (§ 35a SGB VIII).
s.eingl.tip: Apply early and informally. An independent participation advice service (EUTB) can help with the application.
s.pausch.wo: In the income tax return at the Finanzamt. No separate application is needed.
s.pausch.tip: Anyone who uses the allowance cannot deduct the costs it covers again individually.
s.ausweis.wo: At the Versorgungsamt. In Bavaria this is the Zentrum Bayern Familie und Soziales (ZBFS).
s.ausweis.tip: The card is voluntary but opens access to many compensations for disadvantages.
s.blindengeld.wo: In Bavaria at the Zentrum Bayern Familie und Soziales (ZBFS). In other federal states at the office shown above under “Responsible office”.
s.blindengeld.tip: The first application can be informal, oral or by email. Blindengeld is paid from the month of the application at the earliest.
s.pflegeplus.wo: At the Pflegekasse that belongs to your health insurance.
s.pflegeplus.tip: Apply for conversions before the work starts.
s.arbeit.wo: At the provider of integration assistance (in Bavaria usually the Bezirk). Talk to the workshop first.
s.arbeit.tip: The budget is only granted once an employer offers a socially insured employment contract at collective-agreement or locally usual pay.
s.rundfunk.wo: At the Beitragsservice of ARD, ZDF and Deutschlandradio, with the form and the notice of your social benefit.
s.rundfunk.tip: Apply within two months after the notice. The exemption also covers a spouse or registered partner in the same home.
s.zuzahl.tip: Keep all receipts for co-payments. Once the limit is reached, the Krankenkasse issues an exemption for the rest of the year.
s.bab.wo: At the Agentur für Arbeit, online, in writing or in person.
s.bab.tip: Apply before the training starts. If you apply later, payment only starts from the month of application. The BAB calculator of the Federal Employment Agency shows the amount.
s.wbs.wo: At the Wohnungsamt of your municipality or city.
s.wbs.tip: The office calculates the income exactly. Bring proof of income for all household members.
t.kgBeh.keine: For children under 18 the normal Kindergeld applies. This item concerns adults with a disability.
t.kgBeh.nach25: Kindergeld for an adult child with a disability is only paid if the disability began before the 25th birthday. Here it began later.
t.kgBeh.na: You already receive Kindergeld for this child.
t.kgBeh.ja: For an adult child with a disability there can be Kindergeld with no age limit. Condition: the disability began before the 25th birthday and the child cannot support themselves because of it. Kindergeld is {kg} per month. It is the normal Kindergeld, not a second payment on top for the same child.
t.kgBeh.pruefen: Possible if the disability began before the 25th birthday and the child cannot support themselves because of it. The Familienkasse compares the child’s own income with the basic tax allowance ({gfb} in 2026) plus the extra needs caused by the disability. Apply, the Familienkasse will do the calculation.
t.emrente.alter: From the standard retirement age there is no pension for reduced earning capacity any more, but the old-age pension.
t.emrente.keine: A pension for reduced earning capacity is only paid once an adult can work fewer than 6 hours a day because of illness or disability.
t.emrente.voll: Anyone who can work less than 3 hours a day counts as fully incapacitated for earning and gets the full pension.
t.emrente.teil: If you can work 3 to under 6 hours a day, you count as partially unable to work and get half the pension. If no suitable part-time job is found, you may still get the full pension.
t.emrente.ja: According to your information the waiting period is met. The pension insurance first checks whether rehabilitation can restore the ability to work.
t.emrente.werkstatt: People who work in a workshop for people with disabilities are generally treated as fully incapacitated for earning. Instead of the 5-year waiting period, a waiting period of 20 years can be enough. Have this clarified with the pension insurance.
t.emrente.warte: Usually at least 5 years of insurance and 3 years of compulsory contributions in the last 5 years are needed. There are exceptions, for example after a work accident. Have your insurance periods checked by the pension insurance.
t.eingl.keine: No person with a disability was given.
t.eingl.kind: For children with a disability, for example early intervention, school assistance and help with participation can be considered. For a physical or intellectual disability the provider of integration assistance is responsible, for a mental-health disability the Jugendamt (§ 35a SGB VIII). As to assets, cash assets up to 150 % of the annual reference amount are disregarded (§ 139 SGB IX).
t.eingl.erw: People with a substantial disability can receive integration assistance, for example for assistance in daily life, housing, work or participation in education. As to assets, cash assets up to 150 % of the annual reference amount are disregarded (§ 139 SGB IX). The provider examines each case.
t.pausch.keine: The degree of disability is missing for this.
t.pausch.ja: From GdB 20 there is a disability lump-sum allowance in the tax return. For your degree it is {betrag} per year as a deduction from income. How much tax this saves depends on your tax rate.
t.pausch.kind: For a child you can have the allowance transferred to you on request. It is usually split in half between both parents.
t.ausweis.schwer: From a degree of disability of 50 a person counts as severely disabled. Then there is the severe disability card and compensation for disadvantages, for example {tage} days of paid extra leave per year for a 5-day week.
t.ausweis.gleich: With a GdB of 30 or 40 a person does not count as severely disabled. But they can be treated as equal if, because of the disability, they would otherwise not get or keep a suitable job. You apply at the Agentur für Arbeit.
t.ausweis.niedrig: With a GdB below 30 there is no severe disability card and no equal treatment. The disability lump-sum allowance in tax may still apply.
t.ausweis.antrag: The degree of disability has not been determined yet. At the Versorgungsamt you can apply for the degree of disability and markers. Many further forms of help depend on it.
t.blindengeld.keine: No blindness and no severe visual impairment was given.
t.blindengeld.blind: In Bavaria blind people receive Blindengeld: {betrag} per month (as of {stand}).
t.blindengeld.hoch: In Bavaria severely visually impaired people receive Sehbehindertengeld: {betrag} per month (as of {stand}).
t.blindengeld.pflege: At care level {pg} part of the Pflegegeld is offset (Art. 4 BayBlindG): about {kuerz}. The Blindengeld continues to be paid, but then only about {rest} a month (at least {eur:20}).
t.blindengeld.land: This only applies if you live in Bavaria. Other federal states have their own rules and amounts. Ask the responsible state office there.
t.pflegeplus.antrag: A care level has been applied for or is possible. Once it is determined, further benefits from the Pflegekasse come into question.
t.pflegeplus.keiner: Without a care level these benefits are not available.
t.pflegeplus.mittel: With a care level the Pflegekasse pays, for care at home, disposable care aids up to {verbrauch} per month and a grant for home adaptations (for example an accessible bathroom) up to {wohn} per measure.
t.pflegeplus.verh: From care level 2 there is also respite care and short-term care when the carer is unavailable or needs a break. They share one joint annual amount. Ask the Pflegekasse for the current amount.
t.arbeit.keine: The Budget for work is meant for people who work in a workshop for people with disabilities or would be entitled to a place there.
t.arbeit.ja: People who work in a workshop can move to an employer with the Budget for work. The employer receives a wage subsidy of up to {prozent} % of the wage, plus help at the workplace. A socially insured employment contract at collective-agreement or locally usual pay is required.
kids6.label: How many of them are under 6?
kids14.label: How many of them are 14 to 17?
t.fehlt.einkommen: Enter the household’s monthly gross income (0 if there is none). Only then can this benefit be assessed.
t.fehlt.vermoegen: Enter your assets (savings), 0 if you have none.
t.fehlt.miete: Enter your rent, 0 if you pay none.
first.text: SoLo gives guidance. It is not legal advice and does not replace an official decision. The responsible office always decides on your entitlement.
t.rundfunk.mehr: Other grounds for exemption include BAföG, Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe or Ausbildungsgeld (if you do not live with your parents), benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz, Hilfe zur Pflege, Blindenhilfe and deaf-blindness. If you are refused an exemption, you can apply for a hardship exemption; this usually requires a rejection notice first. With the marker RF in the ID card there is a reduction to one third.
t.wbs.abzug: The calculation is simplified. Depending on the case, flat-rate deductions are taken from income (up to 30 %, but each only if you actually pay taxes, health/care insurance or retirement provision), plus allowances, for example {eur:4000} for each severely disabled household member, and a maintenance deduction. The housing authority of your city or municipality makes the exact check.
t.rundfunk.bezug: Anyone who receives Grundsicherung, social assistance or Grundsicherungsgeld can be exempted from the broadcasting fee. This also applies to a spouse or registered partner in the same home.
t.rundfunk.folgt: If you are granted Grundsicherung or Grundsicherungsgeld, you can then be exempted from the broadcasting fee. The same can apply to other social benefits, for example blind assistance.
t.rundfunk.haerte: If your income exceeds the needs threshold of a social benefit by less than the broadcasting fee, you can apply as a special hardship case.
t.rundfunk.nein: According to your information there is no entitlement to exemption. It is mainly granted when receiving certain social benefits.
t.zuzahl.keine: No disability or need for care was given.
t.zuzahl.grenze: For co-payments on medicines, aids and treatments there is a limit of 2 % of the annual gross income for living expenses. Once it is reached, the Krankenkasse issues an exemption for the rest of the year. There are allowances for family members in the household.
t.zuzahl.chron: For people with a serious chronic illness the limit is 1 %. This includes, for example, someone with a GdB of at least 60 who is in continuous treatment. The Krankenkasse decides. Pflegegrad 3 to 5 also counts.
t.bab.keine: Vocational training allowance is for apprentices in a recognised training occupation. A matching entry is missing.
t.bab.wohnen: Vocational training allowance is available if you cannot live with your parents because of the training. From age 18, if married or with a child of your own, this condition is not needed.
t.bab.ja: Possible. The amount depends on your income and the income of your parents or partner. Their income only counts above allowances. The BAB calculator of the Federal Employment Agency shows you the amount. As a rule it must be your first training.
t.wbs.ja: Your gross income is below the limit for subsidised housing in Bavaria: {grenze} per year for your household. The Wohnungsamt calculates exactly (with deductions) and checks further conditions.
t.wbs.rand: Your gross income is above the limit of {grenze} per year, but after deductions for taxes and insurance it may be below. The Wohnungsamt calculates exactly.
t.wbs.hoch: Even with the possible deductions, the income is probably above the limit of {grenze} per year for subsidised housing in Bavaria.
t.ggeld.ausbildung: People in school, studies or training that can be funded through BAföG usually do not get Grundsicherungsgeld, even if no BAföG is actually paid. Exceptions apply only in certain cases, for example evening school or where no BAföG is possible for the school. Certain extra needs, for example in pregnancy or for single parents, are possible. The Jobcenter decides whether an exception applies to you.
t.wohngeld.ausbildung: If everyone in the household is in principle entitled to BAföG or Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe, there is no Wohngeld (§ 20 WoGG). This also applies if the benefit is not paid because of your income or assets. There are exceptions, for example if the training is not eligible for funding. Have this checked at the Wohngeldstelle.
t.wohngeld.keineMiete: You did not enter any rent. Wohngeld is a subsidy towards rent. People living in their own house or flat can get a Lastenzuschuss. Enter your housing costs or ask at the Wohngeldstelle.
t.wohngeld.zuNiedrigVerm: Wohngeld requires a minimum income. Your income probably does not cover living costs and rent. Because of your assets, Grundsicherung is unlikely to be an option. Ask at the Wohngeldstelle whether an application makes sense.
beh.hint: Only open this if it applies: people with a disability, reduced earning capacity or in training.
ov.label: Quick overview of matches
t.wbs.gebiet: Your income is above the general limit of {grenze} per year. In areas with high housing demand the municipality can set higher limits of up to {max}. Ask the Wohnungsamt whether this applies to you.
f.pdfFail: The PDF could not be created. You can share or copy the folder as text instead.
f.pdfArNote: PDF: the document list stays in German (Arabic is not supported in the PDF).
sc.nativeIntro: Take a photo of the form. Recognition runs only on your device; the photo is not sent anywhere and is deleted afterwards. You see what each field means and which answer from your check goes there. The app does not fill in the form itself.
t.land.blindengeld: This blind person's allowance under the Bavarian Blindengeldgesetz exists only in Bavaria. Your federal state has its own state allowance with different rules and amounts. Ask the responsible state office or Versorgungsamt.
t.land.wbs: The app's income limits for the Wohnberechtigungsschein (housing entitlement certificate) apply only in Bavaria. Your federal state has its own limits. Ask the housing authority of your city or municipality.
plz.label: Postcode of your home
plz.hint: The app uses it to find your federal state and rent level. What you enter stays on your device.
plz.notFound: I don't know this postcode. Check your entry, or choose the federal state and rent level yourself.
plz.ask: This postcode has several possibilities with different rent levels. Choose where you live:
plz.unknown: No rent level is stored for this place. Choose it yourself below.
plz.source: Source: Annex to the Wohngeldverordnung, rent levels valid since {stand} (current version). The Wohngeldstelle decides with binding effect.
plz.states: This postcode lies in more than one federal state. Choose your federal state.
bl.label: Federal state
bl.hint: Important for Blindengeld and the Wohnberechtigungsschein. So far the app only calculates these for Bavaria.
plz.altSum: Do you live in a larger municipality of this district?
plz.alt: Your place may belong to a larger municipality that has a different rent level. If so, choose it here.
beh.stelle: Responsible office for where you live:
beh.pruefen: Address from official information (the authority's legal notice or BayernPortal, retrieved {stand}). Please check before sending; offices sometimes move.
beh.ohneAdr: You can find the address on the authority's website.
beh.plzHint: Enter your postcode above and the app will show the responsible office with its address (currently for Bavaria).
beh.fkUnklar: For where you live, the official directory lists Familienkasse Bayern Nord (post: {nord}) or Bayern Süd (post: {sued}). The free Familienkasse service number tells you which one is responsible: {tel}.
f.adrFehlt: To fill in the address of the responsible office, the app needs your postcode (currently for Bavaria). Enter it in the questionnaire above or in your address under "postcode and town", and the app will add the recipients.
unterh.label: Maintenance for the children per month
unterh.hint: What the other parent pays for the children, for all children together. Leave empty if nothing is paid. Do not enter Unterhaltsvorschuss here. Include maintenance for yourself in your income.
t.uvg.teil: The maintenance the children already receive ({u} per month) is deducted. Unterhaltsvorschuss is only paid for the part by which it falls short of the Unterhaltsvorschuss amount.
t.uvg.genug: The children already receive {u} maintenance per month. That is at least as much as Unterhaltsvorschuss; the maintenance paid is fully deducted.
cb.nichtArbeit2: The second person's income does not come from work, for example pension, Arbeitslosengeld I or Krankengeld.
ek.intro: For each adult, enter what they receive per month. Do not enter Kindergeld, Wohngeld or Kinderzuschlag; the app takes them into account itself.
ek.brutto.hint.lohn: Shown at the top of the payslip (total gross). If wages vary: average of recent months.
ek.brutto.hint.rente: Shown in the pension notice: pension before health and care insurance are deducted.
ek.netto: What arrives in your account each month
ek.netto.hint: Leave empty if you don't know. The app then assumes 80 % of the gross.
ek.betrag: Amount per month according to the notice
ek.betrag.hint.alg: Shown in the notice from the Agentur für Arbeit. If a daily amount is given: times 30.
ek.betrag.hint.kg: Shown in the letter from the health insurance fund. If a daily amount is given: times 30.
ek.art.hint: Wages or salary also covers mini-jobs and self-employment. With several incomes (for example pension and a mini-job): choose the largest and enter the total.
lg.gesund.hint: None of this applies? Just continue.
start.1: Answer the questions about your household, your home and your income.
start.2: Your result appears here and updates with every entry.
start.3: Want to see what it looks like first? Load an example above.
warn.netto: The amount paid into your account is higher than gross. This is almost always a typo: please check.
bh.person.hint: Child aged 18+: only if the disability already existed before the 25th birthday (important for Kindergeld). Otherwise choose “an adult”.
bh.gdb.hint: Shown in the notice from the Versorgungsamt or ZBFS, or on the Schwerbehindertenausweis.
geb.label: In what year was the oldest adult born?
geb.hint: For example 1962. This shows whether retirement age has been reached.
warn.geb: Please enter a 4-digit year of birth, for example 1962.
cb.mzG: The Schwerbehindertenausweis shows the marker G or aG
kindEink.label: Children's own income per month
kindEink.hint: For example apprenticeship pay or a mini-job, all children together, the amount paid out. Without Kindergeld and maintenance. Leave empty if none.
legende: Likely: good chance, apply. Possible: worth asking. Amounts are rough estimates; the office calculates the exact amount.
warn.klein: {v} is very little. Please check the number (for example 2,050 instead of 2.05).
warn.gross: {v} is very much. Please check the number.
warn.zahl: Please enter a number only, for example 780.
ek.geschaetzt: Gross is missing. The app estimates it at about {b}. With the real gross amount the result is more accurate.
ek.betrag.hint.eg: Shown in the notice from the Elterngeldstelle. For ElterngeldPlus enter the monthly amount.
bh.em.unklar: Don't know, but sick for a long time
t.schaetz.spanne: Rough estimate: about {a} to {b} per month.
t.schaetz.bis: Rough estimate: up to about {b} per month.
t.pausch.fahrt: In addition there is a travel cost allowance of {betrag} per year.
t.pausch.steuer: This only helps if you pay tax. With a small pension or income it often brings nothing.
t.pausch.laeuft: Once the notice arrives, from GdB 20 there is the allowance in the tax return, also retroactively.
t.ausweis.schwerRente: From a degree of disability of 50 you count as severely disabled. You then get the Schwerbehindertenausweis and compensations, for example discounts.
t.ausweis.g: With marker G you can get a Wertmarke for buses and local trains (free with Grundsicherung, otherwise for an annual fee) or a reduction in vehicle tax.
t.ausweis.laeuft: Your application is already in progress. If the notice is wrong, you can object within one month.
t.emrente.unklar: If you have been sick for a long time, have it checked whether a Erwerbsminderungsrente is possible. The Rentenversicherung checks this, often after rehab. If your Krankengeld ends soon, advice from the Rentenversicherung or a social counselling service helps.
t.gsa.grenz: Whether retirement age has been reached depends on the month of birth. Before that the Jobcenter is responsible.
t.bafoeg.betrieb: There is no BAföG for in-company training, but Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe.
t.bab.kind: The child applies for Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe at the Agentur für Arbeit. It is usually only paid if the child does not live with the parents.
t.but.inhaltKlein: This includes {teil} per month for sport, music or culture, lunch and outings at the Kita.
arbeit.label: Is an adult unemployed, soon unemployed or on sick leave?
cb.algZeit: Worked in insured employment for at least 12 months in the last 30 months (periods with Krankengeld count)
algMon.label: How long in insured employment in total in the last 5 years?
krankW.label: How long on sick leave?
lohnV.label: Last gross pay from work per month
lohnV.hint: For a rough amount of unemployment benefit or Krankengeld. Shown on the last payslip.
s.alg1.wo: Register as a job seeker online, by phone or in person. Register as unemployed in person or online with ID, at the latest on the first day without work.
s.alg1.tip: Register as a job seeker at least 3 months before your job ends. If you find out later, within 3 days. Otherwise a blocking period may apply.
s.krankengeld.wo: The doctor's practice sends the sick note electronically to the health insurance fund. Usually no application is needed.
s.krankengeld.tip: Watch for letters from the health insurance fund: if it asks you to apply for rehab, you have 10 weeks. Get advice first.
u.kuendigung: Notice of termination or contract with end date
u.au: Sick note (certificate of incapacity for work)
t.alg1.na: You already receive it. If it runs out and money is not enough, check Grundsicherungsgeld or Wohngeld in time.
t.alg1.nahtlos: When Krankengeld ends, you may get unemployment benefit even if illness limits your ability to work, while the Rentenversicherung checks (Nahtlosigkeit, § 145 SGB III). Contact the Agentur für Arbeit in good time.
t.alg1.keine: Unemployment benefit is paid after insured employment if you are or become unemployed.
t.alg1.alter: From the statutory retirement age there is no unemployment benefit, but the old-age pension.
t.alg1.zeit: You need at least 12 months of insured employment in the last 30 months. The Agentur für Arbeit checks your periods.
t.alg1.ja: You get {p} % of the standardised net pay of the last 12 months.
t.alg1.dauer: According to your details for about {m} months.
t.alg1.dauerMin: At least 6 months, up to 24 months depending on insurance period and age.
t.alg1.melden: Important: register as a job seeker at least 3 months before the end, otherwise a blocking period may apply. If you resign yourself, there is usually a 12-week blocking period.
t.krank.keine: The health insurance fund pays Krankengeld if you are on sick leave for longer than 6 weeks.
t.krank.lfz: For the first 6 weeks your employer continues to pay your wages. After that the health insurance fund pays Krankengeld: 70 % of gross, at most 90 % of net.
t.krank.ja: The health insurance fund pays Krankengeld: 70 % of gross, at most 90 % of net. Contributions are deducted from it.
t.krank.78: Krankengeld for the same illness is paid for at most 78 weeks within 3 years; the 6 weeks of continued pay count. Plan ahead: afterwards unemployment benefit (Nahtlosigkeit) and a Erwerbsminderungsrente may apply.
t.krank.ende: Krankengeld ends after 78 weeks. Afterwards unemployment benefit (also with limited ability to work) and a Erwerbsminderungsrente may apply. If that is not enough, check Grundsicherungsgeld or Wohngeld.
t.but.azubi: The education package is for children under 18 and for young adults up to 25 who attend school and receive no apprenticeship pay.
beh.pruefenKurz: Please check the address before sending.
ek.betrag.hint.wfbm: Shown on the workshop payslip: the amount paid out.
t.schaetz.mind: Rough estimate: at least {a} per month.
t.gsa.essen: In addition there is an extra allowance for lunch at the workshop.
t.gsa.eltern: If you live with your parents, you get Grundsicherung for yourself alone. Your parents' income does not count (only from 100,000 € a year). A share of the housing costs is added.
t.gsa.heim: In a residential home, Grundsicherung pays the standard rate and housing costs. The Sozialamt settles the housing costs with the home.
t.wohngeld.eltern: If you live with your parents, you belong to their household. Your parents then apply for Wohngeld for everyone. For you alone, Grundsicherung is usually right.
t.wohngeld.heim: In a residential home, Grundsicherung comes first.
t.rundfunk.rf: With the marker RF there is a reduction to one third of the broadcasting fee. With Grundsicherung it is even an exemption.
es.q.geb: In what year were you born?
es.q.mieteEltern: Do you pay rent to your parents?
es.q.miete: How much rent do you pay each month?
es.q.lohn: How much money do you get for your work each month?
es.h.lohn: It is on your payslip. Everything that is paid out.
es.q.essen: Do you eat lunch at the workshop?
es.q.em: Can you only work a little because of your illness or disability?
es.h.em: A little means: less than 3 hours a day.
es.q.renteBetrag: How much pension goes into your bank account?
es.h.rente: Each month. It is on your bank statement.
es.q.ausweis: Do you have a Schwerbehindertenausweis (disability card)?
es.q.gdb: Which number is on your card?
es.h.gdb: The number is called: degree of disability.
es.q.mz: Which letters are on your card?
es.h.mz: Tap all the letters. Then tap Next.
es.q.pflege: Do you have a care level (Pflegegrad)?
es.q.erspart: How much money have you saved?
es.h.plz: Then we can tell you where to go.
es.a.emNein: No, I can work a lot
es.erg.hinweis: This is an estimate. The office calculates exactly. Get help, for example from your legal guardian.
es.n.pflegeplus: More help from the Pflegekasse (care fund)
es.n.zuzahl: Lower co-payments at the health fund
es.r.gsa: Grundsicherung is money to live on. The Sozialamt pays it if your own money is not enough.
es.r.ggeld: This is money to live on from the Jobcenter. It is for people who can work.
es.r.wohngeld: Wohngeld is money for the rent.
es.r.pflege: You get Pflegegeld every month from the Pflegekasse. You can use it to pay for help.
es.r.pflegeplus: The Pflegekasse pays even more: for example gloves and bed pads, or care when your helpers are on holiday.
es.r.emrente: This is a pension for people who cannot work much because of illness or disability. After 20 years in a workshop you can get it.
es.r.rundfunk: Maybe you do not have to pay for TV and radio.
es.r.ausweis: With the card you get help, for example cheaper bus and train travel.
es.r.eingl: Eingliederungshilfe helps you in everyday life: with living, work and free time. In Bavaria the Bezirk pays.
es.r.blindengeld: Blind people get blind allowance every month.
es.r.zuzahl: Maybe you pay less for medicines.
es.r.kgBeh: Your parents can get Kindergeld for you, even if you are an adult. Important: the disability existed before you were 25.
es.r.pausch: If you pay tax, you pay less with the allowance.
es.r.arbeit: With the budget for work you can work at a normal workplace. The employer gets money for it.
es.q.kind: Have you had the disability since childhood?
es.h.kind: That means: the disability existed before you were 25.
es.warn.hoch: Is that right? {v} a month is a lot. If it is right, tap Next again.
es.warn.niedrig: Is that right? {v} a month is very little. If it is right, tap Next again.
es.warn.keineMz: No letters on the card? Then tap: No letters.
es.q.wfbmJahre: How long have you worked in a workshop?
es.h.schon: Tap everything you already get. Then tap Next.
es.schon.eingl: Eingliederungshilfe (for example for the residential home)
es.schon.kg: My parents get Kindergeld for me
es.kopiert: Copied. Now paste it into a message, for example.
es.tipp.wertmarkeFrei: You have H, Bl or TBl on your card? Then you travel free by bus and train. Get the Wertmarke from the Versorgungsamt (in Bavaria: ZBFS).
es.tipp.wertmarkeGsa: With G on your card and Grundsicherung you travel free by bus and train. Get the Wertmarke from the Versorgungsamt (in Bavaria: ZBFS).
es.tipp.wertmarke: With G on your card you can travel cheaply by bus and train. The Wertmarke costs a yearly fee. With Grundsicherung it is free.
es.tipp.b: You have B on your card? Then your companion travels free by bus and train.
es.tipp.rf: You have RF on your card? Then you pay less for TV and radio. With Grundsicherung you pay nothing.
es.tipp.eltern: You live with your parents? Your parents' money does not count. The office also pays part of the housing costs. Ask the Sozialamt.
es.tipp.heim: In a residential home, Grundsicherung also pays the housing costs. A large part goes straight to the home.
es.tipp.essen: You eat lunch at the workshop? There is extra money for this. Say so in the application.
es.tipp.pauschEltern: Your parents can use your tax allowance for themselves. Then they pay less tax.
es.tipp.pauschElternH: Your parents can use your tax allowance for themselves: 7,400 € a year with H, Bl or TBl. Then they pay less tax.
es.tipp.pflegePausch: Your parents care for you? Then they get a care allowance in their tax: 600 € to 1,800 € a year.
es.tipp.kgEltern: Your parents apply for Kindergeld. The letter is written for them.
es.tipp.kgAbzweig: Your parents get Kindergeld for you but give you nothing? Then the Familienkasse can pay the Kindergeld to you (Abzweigung).
t.emrente.wfbm20: After 20 years in a workshop you can get a pension for full reduction in earning capacity. Ask the Rentenversicherung for advice.
t.eingl.na: You already get Eingliederungshilfe. If something changes, tell the office.
ek.weiteres: Do you get a second income?
ek.weiteres.hint: For example workshop pay and a pension. Then choose the second one here.
cb.grundrente33: At least 33 years of pension contributions from work (also a workshop), child-raising or care
cb.wfbmEssen: Eats lunch at the workshop (extra allowance)
es.tipp.wgOderGsa: Wohngeld and Grundsicherung cannot be combined. Ask the Sozialamt which is better for you. With Grundsicherung, bus and train (with G) and the broadcasting fee are often free.
es.tipp.grundrente: If you have 33 years of pension contributions (also workshop years), part of your pension stays free, up to 281.50 €. It is in your pension notice.
t.gsa.grundrente: With at least 33 years of basic pension periods (work, also in a workshop, child-raising, care), part of the pension stays free: 100 € and 30 % of the rest, at most 281.50 € (§ 82a SGB XII). Then Grundsicherung may be possible even with a higher pension.
t.kgBeh.hoch: Own income is well above the basic tax allowance ({gfb} a year) and the disability allowance. Then the person can usually support themselves; Kindergeld is unlikely.
t.ggeld.gemischt: If one person has reached retirement age or is fully unable to work, the Sozialamt is responsible for them. If the other person can work, they and the children belong to the Jobcenter (mixed household). Have both checked.
t.krank.minijob: A mini-job (up to 603 € a month) does not include health insurance through work. It gives no Krankengeld.
t.alg1.minijob: A mini-job (up to 603 € a month) is not unemployment-insured and does not count for unemployment benefit. Earlier jobs with higher pay can count.
alt.hinweis: Note: The rules in this version are as of {stand}. For 2027 only the new minijob limit (633 €) has been added so far. Kindergeld, standard rates, Wohngeld and other amounts may have changed on 1 January. Please update the app.
cb.teilhabe: Gets help for school, training or job preparation because of the disability (e.g. vocational training centre, school assistant). Not: workshop.
bhWeitere.label: Other people in the household with a severe disability
bhWeitere.hint: Only those with GdB 100, or GdB from 50 and a care level. Important for Wohngeld and the Wohnberechtigungsschein.
t.mehr.teilhabe: This includes an extra allowance of {betrag}: 35 % of the standard rate, because the person gets help for school, training or work due to the disability.
t.ggeld.mehrBeh: For a child with a disability aged 15 or over, an extra allowance may be added (35 % with help for school or training, 17 % with marker G). Mention it in the application.
t.ggeld.kindGsa: An adult child who permanently cannot work gets their own Grundsicherung from the Sozialamt, even when living with the parents.
t.pflege.pauschbetrag: Whoever cares for this person at home without pay gets a care allowance of {betrag} a year in their tax return.
cb.schwanger: Someone in the household is pregnant (from week 13)
cb.ernaehrung: Someone needs an expensive diet due to illness (e.g. coeliac disease, cystic fibrosis, severe kidney disease)
cb.warmwasser: Hot water comes from a boiler or instantaneous water heater in the flat (not from the heating)
t.mehr.schwanger: This includes an extra allowance for pregnancy of {betrag} (17 % of the standard rate from week 13).
t.mehr.warmwasser: This includes an extra allowance for hot water from a boiler of {betrag}.
t.mehr.ernaehrung: There is an extra allowance for an expensive diet due to illness. The amount depends on the illness. A medical certificate is needed.
t.mehr.erstausstattung: For pregnancy and birth there is also money for initial equipment (clothing, baby equipment). It is applied for separately.
t.ggeld.schulbuch: If school books have to be bought, the Jobcenter pays for them additionally (in Bavaria school books are usually free).
t.kdu.angemessen: Rent is only covered up to a local limit. If it is higher, the office usually asks you to reduce it only after a transition period.
t.pflege.sach: If a care service provides care, the care fund pays a benefit in kind of up to {sach} a month instead of the care allowance. Both can be combined. For day or night care there is up to {tages} a month in addition. (Pflegekasse, Pflegegeld)
t.pflege.rente: For someone who cares unpaid for at least 10 hours a week on at least 2 days and works at most 30 hours, the care fund pays pension insurance contributions. (Pflegekasse)
t.pflege.steuer35a: For care services and household help there is also a tax reduction of 20 % of the costs, at most 4,000 € a year.
t.pflege.zeit: Relatives can take time off work for care (up to 10 days with care support allowance, care leave up to 6 months, family care leave up to 24 months).
t.pflegeplus.budget: From care level 2 there is respite care and short-term care when the carer is unavailable or needs a break. Both share an annual amount of {betrag}.
t.ausweis.kuendigung: Severely disabled people have special protection against dismissal: the Integrationsamt must agree before a dismissal.
t.ausweis.frei: With H, Bl, TBl or aG you travel free by bus and train (free Wertmarke) and pay no vehicle tax.
t.ausweis.park: With aG or Bl there is a parking permit for disabled parking spaces.
t.zuzahl.fahrt: The health insurance fund pays for trips to outpatient treatment with aG, Bl, H or from care level 3 (with level 3: permanently limited mobility). Get approval first.
t.srente.alter: From the statutory retirement age there is the normal old-age pension.
t.srente.allg: With a degree of disability of 50 or more you can retire earlier if you have 35 years of insurance: without deduction 2 years earlier, with a deduction (up to {abschlag} %) up to 5 years earlier than the statutory retirement age.
t.srente.alter2: With a degree of disability of 50 or more and 35 years of insurance: without deduction from {fj} years and {fm} months, at the earliest from {gj} years and {gm} months with a deduction (up to {abschlag} %). Get advice from the Rentenversicherung.
t.srente.keine: This pension is for people with a degree of disability of 50 or more.
n.srente: Old-age pension for severely disabled people
s.srente.wo: At the Deutsche Rentenversicherung: pension information and advice, then apply about 3 months before the desired start.
s.srente.tip: The degree of disability must be at least 50 when the pension starts. The 35 years include child-raising, care and time in a workshop.
es.r.srente: With a severe disability you can retire earlier. Ask the Rentenversicherung.
aufenthalt.label: Residence status
aufenthalt.0: German, EU or with residence permit
aufenthalt.hint: Important because there are separate benefits for people in the asylum procedure, with a Duldung or obliged to leave.
baby.label: Is a baby here or coming soon?
baby.bald: Yes, a baby is coming soon
egVor.label: Net per month before the birth (of the person getting Elterngeld)
egVor.hint: Average of the 12 months before the birth. Enter 0 if there was no income.
t.eg.keine: Elterngeld is paid after the birth of a child to the parents who care for it.
t.eg.asyl: In the asylum procedure or with Duldung there is usually no Elterngeld. Exceptions exist e.g. with work and certain residence permits. The Elterngeldstelle checks this.
t.eg.ohneBetrag: Elterngeld is 65 to 100 % of net income before the birth, at least {min} and at most {max} a month. Enter the net amount and the app calculates more precisely.
t.eg.ja: Basic Elterngeld: about {basis} a month, up to {monate} months together for both parents (single parents alone). ElterngeldPlus: about {plus} a month for twice as long. Working part-time reduces it proportionally.
t.eg.mutterschaft: Maternity pay in the weeks around the birth is counted towards Elterngeld. Apply at the latest 3 months after the birth; it is only paid 3 months backwards.
t.eg.grenze: There is no Elterngeld if the parents together have more than {grenze} of taxable income a year.
t.hzp.keine: Hilfe zur Pflege (care assistance) is paid if someone needs care (usually from care level 2) and the Pflegekasse and own money are not enough.
t.hzp.verm: Assets above the protected amount must first be used for care.
t.hzp.unter: Income is below the limit of about {grenze} a month. If the Pflegekasse and own money do not cover a care service, day care or a home, the welfare office pays the rest.
t.hzp.ueber: Income is above the limit of about {grenze} a month. With high costs (especially in a care home) Hilfe zur Pflege may still be paid, with an own contribution.
t.hzp.heim: In a care home: own income and assets pay the own share first, then the welfare office. Children only contribute from 100,000 € annual income.
t.asyl.keine: Benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz are for people in the asylum procedure, with Duldung or obliged to leave.
t.asyl.ja: Benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz cover living costs, housing and health care, for children also education and participation. The office calculates the exact amount.
t.asyl.analog: After 36 months in Germany higher benefits similar to social assistance are usually paid (Analogleistungen). Special rules apply to people from Ukraine depending on the date of arrival: ask the Sozialamt or Jobcenter.
t.ggeld.asyl: In the asylum procedure, with Duldung or obliged to leave there is no Grundsicherungsgeld or Grundsicherung, but benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz.
t.wohngeld.asyl: People receiving benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz cannot get Wohngeld.
t.kiz.asyl: Kinderzuschlag requires Kindergeld, which is usually not paid in the asylum procedure.
t.kindergeld.asyl: In the asylum procedure or with Duldung there is usually no Kindergeld. Exceptions exist with certain residence permits. The Familienkasse checks this.
s.elterngeld.wo: At the Elterngeldstelle, in Bavaria at the ZBFS, online or with a form.
s.elterngeld.tip: Plan Elterngeld early: partner months and ElterngeldPlus can extend the period.
s.hzp.wo: At the Bezirk (in Bavaria responsible for care assistance), informally or with a form.
s.hzp.tip: Apply early: care assistance is only paid from the month the office learns about it.
s.asylblg.wo: At the Sozialamt of the city or the Landratsamt where you are registered.
s.asylblg.tip: Apply for education and participation benefits for children at the same time.
es.r.hzp: Not enough money for care? Then the office helps. In Bavaria that is the Bezirk.
t.blh.keine: Blindenhilfe (blind assistance) is paid to blind people with low income and assets.
t.blh.hoch: Blindenhilfe is only for blind people (visual acuity at most 1/50 or an equally severe impairment). It is not paid for severe visual impairment.
t.blh.asyl: People receiving benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz usually only get Blindenhilfe after 36 months (Analogleistungen). Before that the office can help in individual cases.
t.blh.verm: Assets above the protected amount must be used first.
t.blh.unter: Income is below the limit of about {grenze} a month. Then no income has to be used.
t.blh.ueber: Income is above the limit of about {grenze} a month. At most {prozent} % of the income above it is counted, so Blindenhilfe may still be paid.
t.blh.bayern: First you get the Bavarian Blindengeld. It is fully counted against the Blindenhilfe. Blindenhilfe is usually a little higher, so the office pays the difference. The amount rises every year on 1 July with pensions.
t.blh.landAnders: First you get the Landesblindengeld of your federal state. It is fully counted. If it is lower than the Blindenhilfe, the welfare office (Sozialamt) pays the difference.
t.blh.kind: For children under 18, Blindenhilfe is only half as high. Because the Landesblindengeld is counted, usually nothing is left.
t.blh.pflege: With care level 2 to 5, part of the Pflegegeld is counted against the Blindenhilfe.
t.blh.heim: In a care home, Blindenhilfe can be reduced, at most to half.
s.blh.wo: At the Bezirk (in Bavaria), otherwise at the welfare office (Sozialamt). An informal application is enough.
s.blh.tip: Apply for the Landesblindengeld first. Blindenhilfe is only paid from the month the office learns about it.
es.r.blh: Blind and little money? Then you may get a little extra on top of the Blindengeld. In Bavaria at the Bezirk.
t.rundfunk.asyl: People receiving benefits under the Asylbewerberleistungsgesetz are exempted from the broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag) on application. Send the notice to the Beitragsservice.
t.alg1.sperrzeit: If you resign yourself or sign a termination agreement without an important reason, you usually get a blocking period: {wochen} weeks without unemployment benefit (Arbeitslosengeld).
t.alg1.neben: Alongside Arbeitslosengeld you may work less than 15 hours a week. {frei} a month stay free, the rest is counted.
t.kindergeld.mehr: Kindergeld is also paid for children up to 21 registered as unemployed, and up to 25 in voluntary service, while looking for a training place or in a break of at most 4 months between two training periods. After the first training the child may work at most 20 hours a week.
t.blindengeld.landJa: In every federal state blind people receive Landesblindengeld, usually regardless of income. Each state sets the amount: for adults about {von} to {bis} per month, often less for children and older people. The responsible office will tell you the exact amount.
t.blindengeld.hochLand: Only some federal states pay a separate benefit for people with severe visual impairment (for example Bavaria). Ask the responsible office whether it exists in your state.
t.blindengeld.pflegeLand: If you receive Pflegegeld, most states partly count it against the Landesblindengeld.
t.wbs.landJa: Your gross income is even below the nationwide limit ({grenze} per year for your household). No federal state has a lower limit, so a Wohnberechtigungsschein is very likely.
t.wbs.landEigen: Each federal state sets its own income limits for the Wohnberechtigungsschein, often well above the federal values. Whether yours is low enough is calculated exactly (with deductions) by the Wohnungsamt. With a low or medium income it is worth asking.
t.wbs.landStelle: You apply at the Wohnungsamt of your city or municipality. There you will also learn the exact limits in your state.
t.lpg.keine: In Bavaria Landespflegegeld is paid from care level 2.
t.lpg.ja: In Bavaria there is Landespflegegeld from care level 2: {betrag} per year (from {stand}), regardless of income. It is paid in addition to the Pflegegeld from the Pflegekasse.
t.lpg.antrag: You apply once at the Bayerisches Landesamt für Pflege, after that the money comes every year. Apply soon, as there is a deadline; the Landesamt will tell you which one.
t.lpg.pflegeAntrag: As soon as a care level of 2 or more is confirmed, Bavaria also pays Landespflegegeld: {betrag} per year.
t.kindergeld.familiengeld: Bavaria only: For children born up to the end of 2024 there is still Familiengeld until their 3rd birthday ({betrag} per month, from the 3rd child {ab3}) and, with a crèche, up to {krippe} Krippengeld per month depending on income. For children born from 2025 neither exists any more.
t.ausweis.gl: Deaf (marker Gl): Some federal states pay their own Gehörlosengeld, for example Hessen and Sachsen-Anhalt; Bavaria does not. Ask the Versorgungsamt of your state.
cb.mzGl: The Schwerbehindertenausweis shows the marker Gl (deaf)
s.lpg.wo: At the Bayerisches Landesamt für Pflege, online or with a form.
s.lpg.tip: Enclose the Pflegekasse decision on the care level. One application is enough, after that the money comes every year.
es.r.lpg: Care level 2 or more? Then Bavaria pays you money every year.
t.mu.keine: Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity allowance) is paid during the protection period around a birth to employed and unemployed women.
t.mu.ohne: Without work or Arbeitslosengeld there is no Mutterschaftsgeld. With Grundsicherungsgeld, however, there is an additional allowance from the 13th week of pregnancy and money for the first equipment.
t.mu.lohn: During the protection period you keep roughly your previous net pay: up to {tag} per day from the Krankenkasse, the employer pays the rest. If you are privately or family insured, the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung pays a one-off amount of up to {bas} instead.
t.mu.alg: With Arbeitslosengeld the Krankenkasse pays Mutterschaftsgeld in the amount of the Arbeitslosengeld during the protection period.
t.mu.minijob: In a minijob without your own health insurance the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung pays a one-off amount of up to {bas}, plus the employer pays the difference to your net pay.
t.mu.frist: The protection period starts {vor} weeks before the expected date and ends {nach} weeks after the birth ({nachLang} weeks for premature or multiple births or a child with a disability). Apply with the doctor's certificate of the due date, at the earliest 7 weeks before.
t.mu.da: If the child is already born, Mutterschaftsgeld only covers the protection period around the birth. If you have not applied yet, do it soon.
t.mu.wer: This applies to the pregnant person if she is employed herself or receives Arbeitslosengeld.
t.kkg.keine: Kinderkrankengeld is paid when a child under 12 is ill and a parent with statutory insurance cannot work because of it.
t.kkg.ohne: Kinderkrankengeld is for parents with statutory health insurance who work (not in a minijob).
t.kkg.ja: If your child under 12 is ill, you can stay at home: {tage} working days per child and parent per year, at most {max} days. The Krankenkasse pays about {satz} % of net pay, at most {hoechst} per day.
t.kkg.ae: If your child under 12 is ill, you can stay at home: single parents have {tage} working days per child per year, at most {max} days. The Krankenkasse pays about {satz} % of net pay, at most {hoechst} per day.
t.kkg.hinweis: The doctor issues a certificate for the employer and the Krankenkasse. For children with a disability it also applies over 12.
t.but.kita: Kita and childminding are free of charge if you receive Grundsicherungsgeld, Wohngeld, Kinderzuschlag or asylum seeker benefits. Show the notice to the youth office (Jugendamt) or the Kita.
s.mutter.wo: At your Krankenkasse; if privately or family insured at the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (online).
s.mutter.tip: The doctor's certificate of the due date is available at the earliest 7 weeks before the birth. Inform your employer, who pays the top-up.
s.kkg.wo: At your Krankenkasse. The certificate comes from the paediatrician.
s.kkg.tip: Inform your employer on the first day and get the certificate.
